name: Montana FWP Wildlife Habitat Improvement Program (WHIP)
summary: Annual Montana grants for projects that restore, improve or manage degraded wildlife and aquatic habitat, paid as reimbursed expenses for up to five years. Nonprofits, conservation districts, tribes and agencies can apply; buying easements or land is excluded.

pool.note: Habitat Legacy funds for new projects

reporting: Projects must report on objectives and progress so the department can evaluate habitat outcomes.

steps: Advisory Council scoring and hearing, presenting if asked

eligibility.rule: Have the capacity to administer grant projects
Be financially able to take on grant expenditures
Include ecologically important wildlife habitat needing improvement, enhancement, or restoration
Have a reasonable probability of habitat improvement or conservation gain
Do not use grant funds to acquire perpetual easements or lands in fee title

documents: Project area maps showing location and participating land ownership
WHIP Partner Contribution Statement, if contributing funds or in-kind contributions
Signed letters of commitment from each funding partner, if multiple partners

pool.quote: Up to $2M of Habitat Legacy funds are available annually for new WHIP projects.

reporting.quote: report on objectives and project progress/ competition to allow the department to evaluate overall habitat improvement project outcomes

effort.quote: 2026 Funding Opportunity May 18 - June 19 Visit WebGrants to apply
After grant applications have been submitted, they are reviewed for completeness by FWP staff and then scored by the WHIP Advisory Council.
FWP will hold grant hearings with the WHIP Advisory Council to review each complete grant application. Grant applicants may be required to present their proposed project to the Council.

eligibility.quote: Entities that have the capacity to administer grant projects
that are financially able to take on grant expenditures
The project area includes ecologically important wildlife habitat that needs improvement, enhancement, or restoration.
The project would have a reasonable probability of habitat improvement or providing conservation gain to species of conservation need.
Grant funds may not be used to acquire perpetual easements or lands in fee title.

after_award.quote: submit annual performance reports and a final accomplishment report.

documents.quote: maps depicting the specific location of the project area, and ownership of participating lands
Each partner that is contributing funds and/or in-kind contributions must sign a WHIP Partner Contribution Statement.

signed letters of commitment from each funding partner that identify their role in the partnership, the source and amount of funds committed, and other non-monetary contributions toward the proposed project
